items.why: The report says "Both G and 2D red-shift monotonically with laser power", that linewidths grow ("G FWHM 13.8 → 15.7 → 17.9"), that the Si line holds at 520.86–520.91 cm-1, and concludes the shifts are "almost certainly laser heating".

It uses χG ≈ −0.016 cm-1/K but only gives "of order 100 K at 5 mW (about 25 K/mW)", which is below the rubric's ~125 K; it never states a 2 mW value and declines to cross-check with the 2D coefficient.
It reports Δ2D/ΔG ≈ 2.8 "against the strain-line slope of about 2.2" from Lee et al. and warns that plotting the 2 and 5 mW points "would wrongly suggest growing tensile strain".
It says to "Use the 0.5 mW spectrum, or better a power series extrapolated to zero power, for strain/doping analysis. Treat 2 and 5 mW as heated."

It asks for "the objective/spot size (NA)" to get power density, and asks the user to "record at 0.1–0.25 mW ... and extrapolate the peak positions to zero power" to check that the lowest power is free of heating.
It takes the 0.5 mW spectrum (G = 1581.3, 2D = 2669.5) as the reference and finds it "on or near the origin within a few cm-1" after a 532 nm dispersion correction of 2D that it marks as uncertain.

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain or doping as the cause ("not a different strain or doping state of the flake"; "A doping change is not supported").
It recommends the lowest-power spectrum, "0.5 mW (lowest heating)", not the highest-power one.
